title: The Verdict of Windrow House
premise: Dominic Vane, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the mayor's funeral, claiming a body lies in the cathedral's sealed crypt. Following clues hidden in the cathedral's own ledgers, Dominic discovers that Windrow House — the town's founding family estate — has been laundering its crimes through the church records for generations, and that the current patriarch, Edmund Windrow, murdered his brother to protect the secret. As Dominic decodes the ledger with help from disgraced journalist Maren Okafor, he learns the confession was written by his own predecessor, who died under suspicious circumstances twelve years ago. In the climax, Dominic traps Edmund into revealing himself during a public exhibition of the restored ledgers; justice arrives not through the courts, which Edmund controls, but through the town itself, which finally reads what has been filed in plain sight. The novel ends with Dominic sealing the crypt for good and choosing to keep only one secret: his own name in the ledger.
about_author: Petra Brightwater is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was meant to read again. She writes mysteries about quiet people who know too much.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Dominic Vane, POV. Three days after Mayor Aldous Windrow's funeral, an envelope arrives at the cathedral archive containing a confession to murder — postmarked the day after the death. Dominic's orderly world tilts; the emotional beat is dread disguised as curiosity as he realizes the handwriting belongs to his dead predecessor.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. He searches his own filing system for traces of the confessor, Archdeacon Hale, and finds a gap: twelve years ago, an entire folder vanished from the W drawer. The beat is unease — the archive he trusted has been edited, and someone inside did it.

chapters.title: A Locked Crypt and a Patient Man
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. He petitions the chapter to open the sealed crypt, citing structural concerns, and is refused by Dean Croft with unusual speed. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into suspicion — the refusal came too fast to be innocent.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept Asking
chapters.summary: Maren Okafor, POV. A disgraced journalist who covered the original Windrow scandal recognizes Dominic at a memorial reception and tells him about the brother, Thomas Windrow, who 'emigrated' twenty years ago. Beat: reluctant alliance; two people who have both been silenced.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Studying the cathedral's donation ledgers, he notices entries where sums repeat in patterns — dates matching deaths, amounts encoding initials. The beat is intellectual thrill curdling into horror: the church has been bookkeeping for murder.

chapters.title: Windrow House Opens Its Doors
chapters.summary: Edmund Windrow, POV. The new patriarch hosts a charity evening and probes Dominic about the archive, charming and menacing. Beat: power performing generosity; Edmund knows exactly what Dominic has received, and wants him to know it.

chapters.title: What Hale Knew
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. She tracks down Hale's last known associate, a retired verger, who reveals Hale requested the crypt be opened weeks before his fatal fall. Beat: grief and guilt — Hale tried to use the same door Dominic just knocked on.

chapters.title: The Cipher of Tithes
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Decoding the ledger fully, he maps six deaths across forty years, each followed by a 'memorial gift' from Windrow House. Beat: cold clarity — this is generational corruption, and Edmund inherited it like furniture.

chapters.title: Someone Searches My Desk
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Returning at night, he finds his office disturbed and the confession letter gone — but a decoy left in its place, meaning he anticipated the theft. Beat: fear turning to resolve; he is now playing the game deliberately.

chapters.title: The Dean's Debt
chapters.summary: Dean Croft, POV. Flashback-tinged chapter revealing Croft owes Windrow money from a scandal years ago and has been the inside hand all along. Beat: self-justification rotting into shame; complicity explained without excused.

chapters.title: Thomas Is Not Emigrated
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. She obtains exhumation records suggesting Thomas Windrow never left England, and a hospital admission under a false name weeks before his disappearance. Beat: grim confirmation — the crypt theory holds, and time is short because Edmund is selling the house.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. He summons Dominic and offers him the archivist position of his dreams — endowed, permanent, untouchable — if the letter is forgotten. Beat: temptation rendered honestly; Dominic wants exactly what's offered, which makes refusing costly.

chapters.title: The Verger's Second Statement
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The old verger recants under pressure, then privately slips Maren Hale's hidden notebook. Beat: courage passing between small people like a relay baton.

chapters.title: Hale's Notebook
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Hale's notes confirm everything and add one devastating line: 'If I die, look beneath the founder's stone — I put the proof where they would never let anyone dig.' Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Beneath the Founder's Stone
chapters.summary: Dominic and Maren, alternating POV. They gain access during restoration works and find a lead box: photographs, a second ledger, and Hale's sworn statement. Beat: triumph immediately shadowed — they are seen leaving by someone they cannot identify.

chapters.title: Croft Breaks
chapters.summary: Dean Croft, POV. Confronted by Edmund over the missing evidence trail, Croft realizes he is next on the ledger. Beat: terror and a flicker of redemption as he anonymously warns Dominic to run.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive Wing
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. An arson attempt destroys part of the archive — including the decoy evidence Edmund believes is real. Beat: loss and fury, but also the reveal that Dominic moved the true proof days earlier; the fire was aimed at ash.

chapters.title: The Exhibition
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren arranges a public exhibition of the restored medieval ledgers, forcing Edmund to attend to control the narrative. Beat: coiled tension — the trap is set in a room full of witnesses and cameras.

chapters.title: Verdict of the Room
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Climax: Dominic presents the decoded tithe-cipher publicly, reading each death beside its 'gift,' while police — tipped via Croft's anonymous statement — wait outside. Edmund, unraveling, denounces the forgery and then names details only the killer could know. Beat: cathartic exposure; justice outside the law begins inside it.

chapters.title: Opening the Crypt
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. With warrants finally issued, the crypt is opened and two sets of remains found, including Thomas Windrow's. Beat: solemn vindication; the town stands in the rain watching its history come up out of the ground.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Aftermath: Edmund remanded, Croft resigning, the paper publishing Maren's rehabilitation. But the town's complicity — decades of looking away — sits uncomfortably. Beat: sober reflection; exposing one man does not absolve everyone else.

chapters.title: One Last Entry
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Restoring the archive, Dominic finds Hale's final unfinished entry and completes it in his own hand, adding his own name to the ledger of those who knew. He seals the crypt. Beat: quiet identity resolution — Dominic stops being the man who files secrets and becomes the man who chose which one to keep.
